lines.text: [warm] Google ranks the sites other sites link to. Here's how Ryze gets you those links — the Backlink Exchange.

Start with what it actually looks like. This is one of your own articles — and right here, inside the text, is a link out to another site. A coffee roaster. Not a directory, not a comment — a real link inside real content. And somewhere out there, someone else's article links back at you the exact same way.

Here's how it works. [curious] Ryze connects its clients into chains. A linen brand links to your candles. You link to a coffee roaster. Nobody links back to the site that linked to them — so to Google, it just looks like the internet doing its thing. Everyone's domain rating grows.
And you only ever trade with non-competing sites. A candle store never links to another candle store.
Every link you earn lands here — in Mentions, under Backlinks. The page that links to you, the page it points at, month by month.
And the best part — you don't have to set any of this up. [pause] It's already on. The exchange ships enabled in your SEO settings, so you're in the network from day one.

Don't want it? One switch. Flip it off — and you're out. Partners can't see you, nobody links to you, you link to nobody. [curious] But honestly — leave it on. Right now it brings around twenty backlinks a month, and that number keeps growing, because the client network keeps growing.
So — your articles go out, links come back, up to fifty a month on autopilot. [smiling] Your domain gets heavier every week, and you never wrote a single outreach email.
